newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Pena as energy secretary.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Pena as energy secretary.

text.p: Under pressure to add a Hispanic to his Cabinet, President Bill Clinton planned on Friday to nominate his transportation secretary, Federico Pena, as his new energy secretary, White House officials said.

In a last-minute decision characteristic of the president, Clinton chose Pena over Elizabeth Moler, chair of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, in order to add a Hispanic to his Cabinet lineup, the officials said.
The only other Hispanic picked so far for Clinton's second-term Cabinet was Representative Bill Richardson, Democrat-N.M., nominated as U.S. ambassador to the United Nations.

"Let's put it this way," said one official. "If there had not been another appointment for Hispanics, it would have been noticed. The fact is Hispanics came out in very high numbers for the president in the election."

At a noon EST (1700 GMT) ceremony, Clinton also planned to name White House aide Alexis Herman to succeed Robert Reich as labour secretary, after coming under pressure from black groups to appoint more African Americans to his Cabinet, said the officials, who asked not to be identified.

Ending a fiercely fought contest, Clinton chose Herman over Representative Esteban Torres, Democrat-Calif. Hispanic groups had rallied for Torres, while powerful blacks such as civil rights leader Jesse Jackson had pushed Herman. Union groups had fought for former Sen. Harris Wofford, Democrat-Pa.
"The most contentious, long-drawn-out selection was for labour," said one official who asked not to be identified.

In addition, Clinton planned to nominate Federal Highway Administration chief Rodney Slater to replace Pena at transportation, and an assistant secretary of Housing and Urban Development, Andrew Cuomo, to replace Henry Cisneros as HUD secretary.

Slater is a long-time Arkansas colleague of the president and was a Clinton confidant and travelling companion during the 1992 presidential campaign. Cuomo is the eldest son of former New York Gov. Mario Cuomo.

Pena, a former mayor of Denver, Colorado, had come under fire for a statement made in May after the crash of a Valujet airliner near Miami that Valujet was a safe airline. U.S. authorities later grounded Valujet for safety shortcomings, although it has since resumed flying.
But administration officials defended Pena's pick to head the Energy Department, saying he had worked hard to promote airline safety.
"If you look at what he's doing, he's promoted safety in a way no other secretary has," said one defender. He would replace Hazel O'Leary at energy.

Clinton on Thursday offered the chairmanship of the Council of Economic Advisers, a three-member council which performs economic analysis for the president, to Federal Reserve Board Governor Janet Yellen, said one administration official.
Clinton was also expected to name another Hispanic, Aida Alvarez, as his choice to head the Small Business Administration. She has been in charge of federal housing oversight at HUD.

Clinton also planned to reappoint a number of Cabinet officials for his second term, including Education Secretary Richard Riley, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt and Veterans Affairs Secretary Jesse Brown.
